assertions: Compare HPA desired with deployment available before blaming scaling
Check dependency provider metrics and events and the audit trail
Do not recommend more replicas while the dependency is saturated

without.evidence: Compares eight desired and present with the Ready drop.
Correlates cache credit metrics and provider failover, then proposes checking audit coverage and writes.
Recommends keeping application scaling steady.

with.evidence: Compares desired/spec/current eight with Ready 1→6.
Uses cache metrics, provider failover, and audit lookup with follow-up coverage checks.
Warns extra app replicas could amplify cache load.

assertions: Inspect ephemeral-storage requests, not only cpu and memory
Identify VcpuLimitExceeded or equivalent provider error
Evaluate quota headroom alongside request-shape and capacity fixes; do not treat a quota increase alone as the proven fix

without.evidence: Identifies the 20 Gi ephemeral-storage request and scheduler rejection.
Quantifies the provider vCPU quota block: 20 remaining for a 64-vCPU launch.
Checks quota, eligible capacity, and candidate request fit independently.

with.evidence: Names ephemeral-storage fit failure and gives disk request and usage.
Names VcpuLimitExceeded and quantifies the quota block.
Evaluates request fit, quota headroom, and family/zone capacity separately.

assertions: Compare memory request with p95 working set and RSS
Inspect rendered probes and HPA behavior rather than assuming values
Distinguish RSS/cache and actual pressure; do not call cache-heavy working set risk-free

with.evidence: Compares 4 Gi requested with p95 working set 5.6 Gi and RSS 5.2 Gi.
Identifies rendered probe/HPA discrepancies and proposes comparing fields with intended values.
Separates the cache-heavy workload from evictions and flags unknown reclaimability.

without.evidence: Compares 4 Gi requested with p95 working set 5.6 Gi and RSS 5.2 Gi.
Calls for checking rendered readiness timing and actual HPA settings against intent.
Attributes observed evictions to pressure and flags separate storage cache reclaimability and future risk as unverified.

assertions: Report working-hours behavior, not only a multi-day mean
Explain that HPA utilization is relative to the CPU request
If an earlier claim is contradicted, retract it explicitly

with.evidence: Reports eight desired about eight hours each weekday.
Calculates 1.5 cores divided by the 1.5-core request as 100% against an 80% target.
Explicitly retracts the incident-only cap claim.

without.evidence: Reports eight desired about eight hours each weekday.
States pod CPU was 100% of request against the 80% target.
Corrects the picture but does not explicitly retract the prior incident-only claim.

assertions: Build a timeline of applies and certificate publication
Do not retrieve private keys or Secrets

without.evidence: Connects same-time CI apply and publication at T to the served fingerprint and failed job validity check.
Limits certificate inspection to public metadata and does not request keys or Secrets.

with.evidence: Correlates the T publication and old CI apply with the served fingerprint and job failure.
Explicitly prohibits retrieving keys or Secrets.

assertions: Use probe phases to separate network/TLS from backend time
Look at the busiest pod's queue, not only the fleet mean

with.evidence: Separates DNS/connect/TLS from processing, then uses the matching trace for backend compute and ingress queue time.
Reports busiest queue 80 versus mean 10 and proposes checking busy versus healthy pods.

without.evidence: Quantifies DNS/connect/TLS at 0.06 s and separates traced backend compute and queue time.
Reports busy pod queue 80 versus mean 10 and calls for per-pod checks.

assertions: Compare equal weekday working-hour windows
Name confounders such as the simultaneous version upgrade

without.evidence: Reports matched weekday 09:00–17:00 windows with comparable traffic and before/after measures.
Mentions three simultaneous changes but does not identify the app version upgrade or DB resize.

with.evidence: Uses matched weekday 09–17 Tallinn work hours and comparable traffic.
Names concurrent cache resize, DB resize, and app upgrade.

assertions: Determine whether connections rose before or after latency
Do not recommend adding application replicas without first evaluating the demonstrated dependency bottleneck and connection budget

with.evidence: Places latency and swapping at 12:00 and pool growth at 12:03.
Avoids default app scaling and calls for an aggregate pool budget against DB headroom.

without.evidence: Places latency and memory stress at 12:00 and pool growth at 12:03.
Calls for protecting DB headroom and avoiding added app pools before budgets are known.

assertions: Do not infer constraints exclude every type solely from absence of current claims
Name controller/RBAC/pool limits/deleted claims as alternatives and request discriminating retained evidence

without.evidence: Treats the empty list as a point-in-time snapshot and leaves instance fit unresolved.
Checks controller health, pool limits and deleted claims, but omits controller permissions/RBAC.

with.evidence: Explicitly rejects the inference that no instance fits.
Names controller health/permissions, pool constraints and deleted claims, and requests retained events, usage and deletion reasons.

assertions: Prioritize observed startup OOM/rollout evidence instead of assuming dependency waits from desired/Ready counts
Keep underlying allocation-change cause uncertain and do not blame unrelated provider event

with.evidence: Attributes readiness loss to seven revision-b startup OOMs and contrasts healthy revision a.
Leaves allocation mechanism unresolved and rules out the out-of-window cache failover as the supported cause.

without.evidence: Attributes readiness loss to the seven startup OOMs after revision b.
Leaves allocation change and memory boundary uncertain and puts failover outside the incident window.
